newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher in hefty volume.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher in hefty volume.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa recorded a new five-year high in huge volume Thursday which denoted an underlying current of profit-taking, dealers said.
They noted heavyweight stocks did not join the rally, which was fuelled instead by the less liquid blue chips.
"The market is rubbing up against resistance levels, with very selective gains today favoring stocks lagging behind the main index," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.1 percent to 826.12 and floor volume swelled to 52.1 million pesos, the strongest tally in more than three years.
Over-the-counter turnover also picked up to 158 million pesos from 138.4 million Wednesday.
The broad market index firmed 0.7 percent, with winners beating losers 56 to 10 and 20 issues closing flat.

"The international market scenario of low interest rates is creating a framework of stability that allows investors to build up positions in more volatile stocks," Bonanno said. "But these new positions are short, because bolsa conditions are overbought."
The MerVal has grown 1.6 percent so far this week and stands 6.2 percent higher so far in June.
"This market just doesn't want to stop, but I think some stocks may have already topped out near-term, especially leading bank, telephone and oil stocks," another trader said.
The day's best main-tier performer was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which shot up 14.9 percent on fresh rumors of a company buy-out or drastic streamlining plan, dealers said.
Other top MerVal risers were gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which jumped 2.9 percent, and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas and carmaker Ciadea, both up 2.6 percent.
Blue-chip losers were led by construction stock Polledo, which shed 1.7 percent, and Banco Frances and oil company Astra, both off 0.7 percent.
